en: Passing or disappearing with time; transitory.

Something that is transient.

en: An official who presides over a sports match.

To act as an umpire in a game.
To decide as an umpire.

ex.ja: 今日では審判になるのは容易ではない。

To lament; to complain.
A session of crying.
A sob.

To pull or twist violently.
To injure (a joint) by pulling or twisting.

ex.ja: 自分の思春期を振り返ると、いつも憂うつな気分になる。

note.ja: ラテン語 adolescere（成長する）から。「思春期」。adolescent と同じ。

en: To agree, verify or concur; to answer positively.
To assert positively; to tell with confidence; to aver; to maintain as true.
Yes; true; correct.

affirm.ety: From Middle English affermen, from Old French afermer, affermer, from Latin affirmare, adfirmare (“to present as fixed, aver, affirm”), from ad (“to”) + firmare (“to make firm”), from firmus (“firm”). By surface analysis, af- + firm.

A cocktail containing vodka, triple sec, lime juice and cranberry juice.

cosmopolitan.ety: From cosmopolit(e) + -an. Compare metropolitan and megalopolitan.

ex.en: The journalist is what you call a cosmopolitan.
ex.ja: そのジャーナリストはいわゆる国際人だ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kosmos（世界）+ politēs（市民）。「世界市民の」→「国際的な」。politics と同じ。

en: Canis latrans, a species of canine native to North America.
A smuggler of undocumented immigrants across the land border from Latin America into the United States of America.
To prospect for gold by manually digging holes into overlying earth, as into a hillside.

coyote.ety: Borrowed from Spanish coyote, from a Nahuan language, from Proto-Nahuan *koyoo-tl. Compare Chinook ki-o-tī.

note.ja: ナワトル語（アステカの言語）coyotl からスペイン語を経た語。

en: That cripples or incapacitates
Causing a severe and insurmountable problem; detrimental.
The act by which somebody or something is crippled.
To furnish with decorations.
To improve the appearance of an interior of, as a house, room, or office.

decorate.ety: From Middle English decorat (“adorned”), from Latin decorātus, perfect passive participle of decorō (“to adorn, distinguish, honor”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from decus (“ornament, grace, dignity, honor”, decor- in compounds), akin to decor (“elegance, grace, beauty, ornament”), from decet (“adorn, befit”).

ex.en: I like to decorate my room with flowers.
ex.ja: 私は部屋を花で飾るのが好きだ。

ex.en: My wife showed excellent taste in decorating the room.
ex.ja: 私の妻は部屋を飾るときに優れた美的感覚を発揮した。

ex.en: I like to decorate my apartment to suit my taste.
ex.ja: 私は好みに合わせてアパートを飾るのが好きです。

note.ja: ラテン語 decorare（飾る）から。decus（飾り）。「飾る・勲章を与える」。decoration と同じ。

An amount of expenses that must be paid out of pocket before an insurer will pay further expenses.

ex.ja: 学校に対するあなたの寄付は、所得控除の対象になる。

en: Joining two nonadjacent vertices (of a polygon or polyhedron).
Having slanted or oblique lines or markings.
A line joining non-adjacent vertices of a polygon.
A line or plane at an oblique angle to another.

diagonal.ety: From Middle French diagonal, from Latin diagōnālis, from Ancient Greek διαγώνιος (diagṓnios, “from angle to angle”), from διά (diá, “across”) + γωνία (gōnía, “angle”).

ex.en: Cut the cloth in a diagonal direction.
ex.ja: 布を斜めに裁ちなさい。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 diagōnios ＝ dia（通して）+ gōnia（角）。「角から角へ通る」→「対角線の」。pentagon と同じ gōnia。

An item of bedroom furniture, like a low chest of drawers (bureau), often with a mirror.

ex.ja: 鏡は鏡台の上にあります。

ex.ja: 「携帯、どこかしら？」「鏡台の上だよ！」

Wood from an elm tree.

elm.ety:
From Middle English elme, elm, from Old English elm, from Proto-West Germanic *elm, from Proto-Germanic *elmaz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁élem (“mountain elm”).
See also dialectal Low German Elm, dialectal German Ilm, archaic German Ilme, Norwegian and Swedish alm; also Irish leamh, Latin ulmus, Albanian ulzë (“maple”).

note.ja: 古英語 elm から。ラテン語 ulmus と同じ祖先。「ニレ」。

enquiry.ety: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). en: Marked by or having equity.
Fair, just, or impartial.

equitable.ety: From French équitable, from Old French, from equité (“equity”).

ex.en: They argue that the distribution of wealth should be equitable.
ex.ja: 富の分配は公平でなければならないと彼らは言う。

note.ja: equity（公平）+ -able。ラテン語 aequus（等しい）。「公平な」。equal と同じ。

en: To make use of, to apply, especially of something nonmaterial; to bring to bear.
To put in vigorous action.

exert.ety: From Latin exsertus, past participle of exserō (“to stretch or thrust forth or out”), from ex- + serō (“to string together”).

ex.en: You should exert yourself to get better results.
ex.ja: もっといい成績を得るように努力しなさい。

ex.en: Several politicians exerted strong pressure on the committee.
ex.ja: 数人の政治家が委員会に強い圧力をかけた。

ex.en: He exerted himself to solve the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題を解こうと努力した。

note.ja: ラテン語 exserere（突き出す）から。ex + serere（つなぐ）。「（力を）出す・行使する」。insert と同じ。

en: The condition of being happy.
Intense happiness.

felicity.ety: From Middle English felicite (“bliss, happiness, joy; delight, pleasure; a source of happiness; good fortune; prosperity; well-being; of a planet: in an influential position”) [and other forms], borrowed from Old French felicité (modern French félicité (“bliss, happiness; felicity”)), from Latin fēlīcitātem, the accusative singular of fēlīcitās (“fertility, fruitfulness; happiness, felicity; good fortune; success”), from fēlīx (“happy; blessed, fortunate, lucky; fertile, fruitful; prosperous; auspicious, favourable”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁(y)- (“to nurse, suckle”)) + -itās

note.ja: ラテン語 felicitas（幸福）から。felix（幸運な）。「至福」。Felix（人名：幸運な人）と同じ。

en: Of, or relating to feudalism.

feudal.ety: From Old French feodal, from Medieval Latin feodalis, from feodum, feudum, fevum (“fief, fee”), from Frankish *fehu (“cattle, owndom, property, fee”), from Proto-Germanic *fehu (“cattle”). By surface analysis, feud (“estate”) + -al. More at fee.

ex.en: It seems a bit feudal to call him "sir".
ex.ja: 彼を「サー」と呼ぶのは少し封建的に思える。

ex.en: In feudal Japan, the lord with the largest land holdings was called a "daimyo."
ex.ja: 日本の封建時代には、最大の土地を所有した領主は「大名」と呼ばれた。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 feudum（封土）から。「封建的な」。fee（料金・封土）と同じ語源。

en: Made flat by something.
Hair or wool of a sheep or similar animal.
Insulating skin with the wool attached.
To con or trick (someone) out of money.
To cut off the fleece from (a sheep or other animal).

fleece.ety: From Middle English fles, flees, flese, from Old English flēos, flīes, flȳs, from Proto-West Germanic *fleus.

ex.en: Mary had a little lamb, whose fleece was white as snow.
ex.ja: メリーさんは、雪のように真っ白な毛をした子羊を飼っていました。

ex.en: Mary had a little lamb whose fleece was white as snow.
ex.ja: メリーさんは、雪のように真っ白な毛をした子羊を飼っていました。

note.ja: 古英語 flēos（羊毛）から。「羊毛」→ 羊毛を刈るように金を巻き上げる →「だまし取る」。

en: Food for animals; that which is fed to cattle, horses, and sheep, such as hay, cornstalks, vegetables, etc.
A load: various English units of weight or volume based upon standardized cartloads of certain commodities, generally around 1000 kg.

fodder.ety:
From Middle English fodder, foder, from Old English fōdor (“feed; fodder”), from Proto-West Germanic *fōdr, from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą, from *fōdô (“food”), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- (“to guard, graze, feed”).
Compare Saterland Frisian Fodder, West Frisian foer, Dutch voer (“pasture; fodder”), German Futter (“fodder; feed”), Danish foder, Swedish foder. More at food.

note.ja: 古英語 fōdor（飼料）から。food、feed と同じ祖先。「飼料」→ cannon fodder（使い捨ての兵）。

en: To handle nervously or awkwardly.
To grope awkwardly in trying to find something
The dropping of a ball by accident.
A clumsy sexual encounter.

Possibly has (a more or less unconscious) connection to fathom (via Old Norse faðmr, Swedish famn) in the

ex.en: She fumbled with a piece of paper.
ex.ja: あやふやな手つきで一枚の紙を動かした。

ex.ja: 怪しげな手つきで彼女はグラスを運んできた。

en: An attack of uncontrolled giggling.
An intense, blinding light.
Showy brilliance; gaudiness.

To shine brightly.
smooth and bright or translucent; glary

glare.ety: From Middle English glaren, from Old English *glærian, from Proto-West Germanic *glarōn. Cognate with dialectal Middle Dutch glariën (“to glisten; sparkle”), Low German glaren (“to shine brightly; glow; burn”), Middle High German glaren (“to shine brightly”). Related to glower, glass.

ex.ja: 彼女は眼を怒らせて私をにらみ付けた。

A connoisseur in eating and drinking; someone who takes their food seriously.

note.ja: フランス語 gourmet（ワインの鑑定人）から。「食通」。

To perform a handshake; to shake hands.
To perform a handshake with another device.

handshake.ety: From hand + shake. See the appendix for the history of the gesture itself.

ex.en: He has a good firm handshake.
ex.ja: 彼はしっかりとした握手をする。

ex.en: He put out his hand to me for a handshake.
ex.ja: 彼は握手を求めて手を差し出した。

ex.en: When my father was offered a golden handshake, he took it.
ex.ja: 僕の父は早く退職するよう退職金を差し出されて受け取ったんだ。

note.ja: hand（手）+ shake（振ること）。「握手」。

Strong; bulky.

hefty.ety:
19th century. From heft (“weight”) + -y.
The similarity with German heftig (“vigorous, violent, intense”) is apparently coincidental. From the German are Dutch, Danish, Norwegian heftig, Swedish häftig.

Made from natural herbs specifically as opposed to from synthetic materials.
A manual of herbs and their medical uses.
An herbal supplement.

ex.en: If you continue to take this herbal medicine, it will do you good.
ex.ja: この漢方薬を飲み続ければ効くでしょう。

To carry (something), especially with some exertion.

ex.ja: この仕事には憂鬱になる。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「こぶ」。over the hump（峠を越えて）。

Romantic relationships between close relatives, also widely taboo.
To engage in incestuous sexual activities.

incest.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin incestus. Displaced Old English mǣġhǣmed (literally “relative-sex”). Doublet of inchaste.

ex.en: Incest is a taboo found in almost all cultures.
ex.ja: 近親相姦はほとんど全ての文化において禁忌とされている。

note.ja: ラテン語 incestus（不浄な）から。in（否定）+ castus（純潔な）。chaste と同じ。

To contaminate (an object or substance) with a pathogen.

infect.ety: From Middle French infect, from Latin infectus, perfect passive participle of inficiō (“dye, taint”).

ex.en: Infect the area with cholera.
ex.ja: コレラで地域を汚染する。

note.ja: in（中に）+ fect（作用する）。中に入り込んで作用する →「感染させる・影響する」。

the act of breaking into someone else’s speech.

interruption.ety: From Middle English interrupcioun, from Old French interrupcion, from Latin interruptio.

ex.en: I was annoyed with him for his interruptions.
ex.ja: 彼が度々口をはさむので腹がたった。

ex.en: Sorry for the interruption.
ex.ja: お邪魔しました。

ex.en: Discussion resumed after a short interruption.
ex.ja: ちょっと中断したあとで討議が再び始まった。

To conceive or carry out a secret plan intended to harm; to form a plot or scheme.
To arouse the interest of; to fascinate.

intrigue.ety: Borrowed from French intrigue, from Italian intricare, from Latin intrīcō (“to entangle, perplex, embarrass”). Doublet of intricate.

ex.en: Foreign people intrigue me.
ex.ja: 外国人って面白いなあ。

ex.en: He watches for an opportunity to intrigue against his rival.
ex.ja: 彼は競争相手を落とし入れようと虎視眈々としている。

en: A sensation felt on an area of the skin that causes a person or animal to want to scratch said area.
A constant teasing desire or want.
To feel itchy; to feel a need to be scratched.
To have a constant, teasing urge; to feel strongly motivated; to want or desire something.

itch.ety: From Middle English icche, ȝicche, from Old English ġiċċe (“itch”), from Proto-Germanic *jukjǭ (“itch”), of unknown origin. Cognate with Scots yeuk (“itch, itchiness”), Dutch jeuk (“itch”), German jucken.

ex.en: She had an itch to see her child.
ex.ja: 彼女は子供に会いたくてたまらなかった。

ex.en: My leg itches. I think something bit me.
ex.ja: 足が痒いよ。何かに噛まれたみたい。

ex.en: I have an itch in my ear.
ex.ja: 耳がかゆいのです。

To close, as an opening, with latticework; to furnish with a lattice.

en: One who designs and executes marketing campaigns.
One who sells products or services, for example goods at a market; called a marketeer in UK English.

marketer.ety: From market + -er (occupational suffix) or + -er (agent noun suffix).

en: A person with an extraordinary intellect or skill that is markedly superior to their peers.
A person responsible for the highest level of planning and execution of a major operation.
To plan or execute (a project) in the role of mastermind.

ex.en: I think overestimating the people masterminding that conspiracy is exactly what they want.
ex.ja: その陰謀を画策してる人たちを必要以上に大きく見てしまうことは、まさに彼らの思うツボだと思います。

note.ja: master（名人）+ mind（頭脳）。「首謀者・立案者」。

en: Data that describes other data, serving as an informative label.
Structured information about a file (date created, creator, software used to create, last modified, file format, file fingerprint, etc).

en: Conduct that playfully causes petty annoyance.
A playfully annoying action.

mischief.ety: From Middle English myschef, meschef, meschief, mischef, from Old French meschief, from meschever (“to bring to grief”), from mes- (“badly”) + chever (“happen; come to a head”), from Vulgar Latin *capare, from Latin caput (“head”).

ex.en: We stopped the child from getting into mischief.
ex.ja: 私たちはその子供がいたずらをするのをやめさせた。

ex.en: Children are always doing some mischief or other.
ex.ja: 子供はいつもなにかしらいたずらをしている。

ex.en: He must have done it out of mischief.
ex.ja: 彼はいたずら半分にそれをしたにちがいない。

note.ja: 古フランス語 meschief（不運）から。mes（悪く）+ chief（頭・結果）。「悪い結末」→「いたずら・害」。

en: The act, process, or result of modernizing.

ex.en: Central to this issue is the problem of modernization.
ex.ja: 論点の中心は、近代化という問題である。

ex.en: In most cases, modernization is identified with Westernization.
ex.ja: ほとんどの場合、近代化は西欧化と同一のものとみなされる。

note.ja: modernize（近代化する）+ -ation。ラテン語 modo（たった今）。「近代化」。

en: A brass or copper pan used to evaporate salt water to obtain salt.

From Neptune (“Roman god of earthquakes and the ocean”).

ex.en: Neptune is dark, cold, and very windy.
ex.ja: 海王星は暗く寒く、かつ烈風が吹き荒れている。

ex.en: Neptune is the eighth planet of the solar system.
ex.ja: 海王星は太陽系の8番目の惑星だ。

ex.en: Bacchus has drowned more men than Neptune.
ex.ja: 酒の神は、海の神より多くの人をおぼれさせた。

note.ja: ローマ神話の海の神ネプトゥヌス（Neptunus）から。「海王星」。

nerd.ety:
Unknown. Attested since 1951 as US student slang.
* Perhaps an alteration of nerts (“nuts", "crazy”); see references below.
* The word, capitalized, appeared in 1950 in Dr. Seuss’s If I Ran the Zoo as the name of an imaginary animal:
*: And then, just to show them, I’ll sail to Katroo / And bring back an It-Kutch, a Preep and a Proo, / A Nerkle, a Nerd and a Seersucker too!
* Possibly a rebracketing of inert as a nert, as in he's inert = he's a nerd, in reference to one's lack of competence or athletic ability.
* Various unlikely folk etymologies and less likely backronymic speculations also e

ex.en: I'm a train nerd, you see.
ex.ja: 電車オタクなんです。

ex.en: Tom is a railway nerd.
ex.ja: トムは鉄道オタクだ。

ex.en: Tom is a language nerd.
ex.ja: トムは言語オタクだ。

en: In a noticeable way.
To a detectable degree, sufficient to be noticed.

noticeably.ety:
Etymology tree
English noticeable
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English noticeably
From noticeable + -ly.

ex.en: It has become noticeably colder.
ex.ja: めっきり寒くなった。

ex.en: I don't like eating pineapples. They have a noticeably sour taste.
ex.ja: パイナップルを食べるのって、好きじゃないのよね。酸味が強いでしょ。

en: The act of occupying, the state of being occupied or the state of being an occupant or tenant.
The period of time during which someone rents or otherwise occupies certain land or premises.
The branch of medicine concerned with tumors, including study of their development, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

oncology.ety: First attested 1857. By surface analysis, onco- + -logy.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 onkos（塊・腫れ）+ logia（学）。「腫瘍学」。

en: The transfer of a business function to an external service provider.

note.ja: out（外に）+ source（調達する）+ -ing。「外部委託」。

en: To defeat an enemy and invade in great numbers, seizing the enemy positions conclusively.
To infest, swarm over, flow over.
An instance of overrunning.
A turnover: a break to a new line by text flowing within the column.

overrun.ety:

From over- + run.

ex.en: We overran the budget by about 5,000 yen.
ex.ja: 予算が足りず、五千円ほど足が出た。

en: Land, specifically, an open field, on which livestock is kept for feeding.
Ground covered with grass or herbage, used or suitable for the grazing of livestock.
To move animals into a pasture.
To graze.

ex.en: There are a lot of sheep in the pasture.
ex.ja: 牧場には羊がたくさんいる。

ex.en: The pasture has an area of 10 acres.
ex.ja: その牧場は１０エーカーの広さだ。

ex.en: A cowboy is driving cattle to the pasture.
ex.ja: カウボーイが牛を牧草地へ追っていく。

note.ja: ラテン語 pastura（放牧）から。pascere（食べさせる）。「牧草地」。pastor（羊飼い → 牧師）と同じ。

Relating to, amounting to, or caused by a physical or mental disorder.

en: That part of a cargo that produces revenue.
The total weight of passengers, crew, equipment, and cargo carried by an aircraft or spacecraft.

payload.ety: From pay + load. From the early 20th century.

note.ja: pay（払う）+ load（荷）。「運賃を払う積み荷」→「有効荷重・搭載量」。

en: An amount of money paid out.
The value of dividends paid to shareholders.
A right that attaches to land, in Scots law.
Important with regard to (a subject or matter); pertaining; relevant.

pertinent.ety: Inherited from Middle English pertinent, borrowed from Old French pertinent and Latin pertinēns, pertinentem.

ex.en: Computer technology is indispensable to access many pertinent items of data.
ex.ja: データの多数の関係項目にアクセスするにはコンピューター・テクノロジーが不可欠である。

ex.en: As for the theoretical side, Peterson's claim is pertinent to our discussion.
ex.ja: 理論的側面については、ピーターソンの主張は我々の議論に直接関係がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 pertinere（関わる）から。per + tenere（保つ）。「関連のある」。contain と同じ ten。

en: Existing in large number or ample amount.
Yielding abundance; fruitful.

plentiful.ety: From Middle English plentiful, plentyfull, plentefull, equivalent to plenty + -ful.

ex.en: We have a plentiful supply of water.
ex.ja: 我々は、水をたくさん持っている。

ex.en: Wolves live in areas where game is plentiful.
ex.ja: オオカミは獲物が豊富な地域に住んでいる。

ex.en: She shed plentiful tears when her beloved dog was killed in an accident.
ex.ja: 彼女はかわいがっていた犬が事故で死んだ時、たくさんの涙を流した。

note.ja: plenty（たくさん）+ -ful。ラテン語 plenus（満ちた）。「豊富な」。plenary（全員出席の）と同じ。

en: One who furnishes, fits, and repairs pipes and other apparatus for the conveyance of water, gas, or drainage.
In the Royal Navy, an apprentice, a boy aged 16 to 18, who is trained in technical skills at the Dockyard Schools to become an artificer.

plumber.ety:
From Middle English plumber, from Old French plummier (French plombier); from Latin plumbārius, from plumbum (“lead or lead shot”).
The verb sense “to botch” is perhaps from the negative stereotype of the occupation.

ex.en: Tom is a self-employed plumber.
ex.ja: トムは自営の配管工だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 plumbarius（鉛細工師）から。plumbum（鉛）。昔の水道管は鉛製 →「配管工」。plumbing と同じ。

en: A measure of the scarcity of an object.
Thinness; the property of having low density

rarity.ety: From rare + -ity, borrowed from Middle French rarité, from Latin rāritās; compare French rareté. See also rare.

en: Showing rebellion.

rebellious.ety: From Middle English rebellious; equivalent to rebel + -ious.

ex.en: Children have a tendency to become rebellious.
ex.ja: 子供は反抗期になる傾向がある。

note.ja: rebellion（反乱）+ -ous。re（再び）+ bellare（戦う）。「反抗的な」。bellicose（好戦的な）と同じ bell。

en: A (typically scaly and egg-laying) cold-blooded vertebrate tetrapod animal, of the class Reptilia (excluding birds), such as a lizard, tu…
Any member of the class Reptilia, including birds.
Creeping; moving on the belly, or by means of small and short legs.
Grovelling; low; vulgar.

reptile.ety: From Middle English reptil, from Old French reptile, from Late Latin rēptile, neuter of reptilis (“creeping”), from Latin rēpō (“to creep”), from Proto-Indo-European *rep- (“to creep, slink”) (Pokorny; Watkins, 1969).

ex.en: I can't stand reptiles.
ex.ja: 爬虫類が大嫌い。

ex.en: My son thinks that bats are reptiles because they're like pteranodons.
ex.ja: 息子は、コウモリはプテラノドンの仲間で爬虫類だと思っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 reptilis（這う）から。repere（這う）。「爬虫類」。

en: To visit again.
To reconsider or reexperience something.
An act of revisiting; a second or subsequent visit.

revisit.ety: From Middle English revisite, from Middle French revisiter and Latin revīsitāre. By surface analysis, re- + visit.

ex.en: I wish to revisit England before I get too old.
ex.ja: 年を取りすぎないうちにまた英国へ行きたい。

note.ja: satire（風刺）+ -ical。ラテン語 satura（ごった煮）。「風刺的な」。

en: Inducing pleasurable or erotic sensations.
Of or pertaining to the physical senses; sensory.

sensual.ety: From Late Latin sensualis (“endowed with feeling, sensual”), from Latin sensus (“feeling, sense”).

ex.en: Great men are fond of sensual pleasures.
ex.ja: 英雄色を好む。

ex.en: They gave themselves up to the enjoyment of sensual pleasures.
ex.ja: 彼らは官能的快楽にふけった。

note.ja: sens（感じる）+ ual。感覚の →「官能的な・肉体的な」。sensory（感覚の）と区別。

en: To collapse heavily or helplessly.
To decline or fall off in activity or performance.
A heavy or helpless collapse; a slouching or drooping posture; a period of poor activity or performance, especially an extended period.
A period of poor performance.

slump.ety: Probably of North Germanic origin: compare Danish slumpe (“to stumble upon by chance”), Norwegian slumpe (“happen by chance”), Norwegian slumpa (“happen by chance”), Swedish slumpa (“randomize; to sell off”), Swedish slump (“chance, randomness, happenstance”). Compare also German schlumpen (“to trail; draggle; be sloppy”), dialectal Dutch slompen (“to walk clumsily”).

ex.en: He seems to be in a slump.
ex.ja: 彼はスランプのようです。

ex.en: The man slumped to the floor.
ex.ja: その男は床にどさっと倒れた。

ex.en: The company is caught up in a serious business slump.
ex.ja: 会社は深刻な営業不振に陥っている。

note.ja: 擬音的な語とされる。「どさっと落ちる」→「急落・不振」。

en: To make something soft or softer.
To undermine the morale of someone (often soften up).

soften.ety: From Middle English softenen, softnen, equivalent to soft + -en.

ex.en: His anger towards me has not softened.
ex.ja: 私に対する彼の怒りは和らいでいない。

note.ja: soft（柔らかい）+ -en。「柔らかくする・和らげる」。t は発音しない。

en: An item of sentimental value, that is given or kept to remember an event or location.
To take (something) as a souvenir, especially illicitly, for example during wartime.

souvenir.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French souvenir (literally “memory”). Compare memento.

ex.en: I'm going to buy souvenirs for my family.
ex.ja: 家族にお土産を買います。

ex.en: Is there a souvenir shop in the hotel?
ex.ja: ホテルの中に土産品店はありますか？

ex.en: What did you buy as a souvenir?
ex.ja: お土産は何買ったの？

note.ja: フランス語 souvenir（思い出す）から。ラテン語 subvenire（心に浮かぶ）、sub + venire（来る）。「記念品」。

en: A manned vehicle that flies through space.
A finite pattern that reappears after a certain number of generations in the same orientation but in a different position.

spaceship.ety:
* space + ship
* (programming operator): From its resemblance to the shape of a flying saucer.

ex.en: The spaceship was never to return to Earth.
ex.ja: その宇宙船は２度と地球に戻れない運命になった。

ex.en: The next morning found him on a spaceship.
ex.ja: 翌朝、彼は宇宙船に乗っていた。

ex.en: Seen from a spaceship, the Earth looks blue.
ex.ja: 宇宙船から見ると、地球は青く見える。

note.ja: space（宇宙）+ ship（船）。「宇宙船」。

en: A person from Spain or of Spanish descent.
A member of the predominant ethnic group of Spain.

Spaniard.ety: From Middle English Spaignarde, from Old French Espaignard, from Espaigne. Equivalent to Spain + -ard.

ex.en: Spaniards love to stroll around in the evening cool.
ex.ja: スペイン人は夜の涼しさの中を散歩するのが大好きだ。

note.ja: Spain + -ard。「スペイン人」。Spanish（スペインの・スペイン語）と区別。

en: Having widely spaced intervals.
Not dense; meager; scanty

note.ja: ラテン語 sparsus（まき散らされた）から。spargere（まく）。「まばらな」。

en: A vessel in which articles are subjected to the action of steam, as in washing and in various processes of manufacture.
A cooking appliance that cooks by steaming.
To travel by steamer.

steamer.ety: From steam + -er. The steamer duck or steamer (sense 6.2) is apparently named for its resemblance to a paddle steamer when swimming rapidly. The feces sense comically evokes the idea of steaming hot food and probably reflects that fresh feces sometimes give off visible water vapor in cold outdoor conditions such as those encountered by hunters, campers, and soldiers.

ex.en: The steamer is now out of sight.
ex.ja: 汽船は見えなくなった。

ex.en: The steamer wound in and out among the islands.
ex.ja: 船は島々の間を見えつ隠れつして縫うように進んで行った。

ex.en: As luck would have it, a steamer passed by and they were saved.
ex.ja: 運よく汽船が通りかかって彼らは救助された。

note.ja: steam（蒸気）+ -er。「蒸気船・蒸し器」。

en: That receives a subsidy.
A force which pushes matter from one space into another because the pressure inside the second space is lower than the pressure in the fi…
A force holding two objects together because the pressure in the space between the items is lower than the pressure outside that space.
To create an imbalance in pressure between one space and another in order to draw matter between the spaces.
To draw out the contents of a space.

suction.ety: From Latin sūctiō, sūctiōnem (whence -ion), attested since Late Latin and derived from sūctus, past participle of sūgō (“to suck”). Attested in English since the early 17th century.

note.ja: ラテン語 sugere（吸う）から。「吸引」。suck と同じ祖先。

en: Any plant of the genus Helianthus, so called probably from the form and color of its floral head, having the form of a large disk surroun…
The commonly cultivated species, Helianthus annuus, a native of America.

sunflower.ety: From sun + flower. Compare English sunbloom.

ex.en: The rain destroyed the sunflower garden.
ex.ja: 雨でひまわり畑は台無しだ。

ex.en: Be careful when carrying sunflower oil.
ex.ja: ひまわり油を運ぶ際は、注意してください。

ex.en: Tom plants sunflowers every spring.
ex.ja: トムは毎年春にひまわりを植えます。

note.ja: sun（太陽）+ flower（花）。「ヒマワリ」。

en: Additional; added to supply what is wanted.
Something additional; an extra.

ex.en: Supplementary information includes adverbs and things that function as adverbs.
ex.ja: 補足情報には、副詞や副詞のはたらきをするものが入ります。

note.ja: supplement（補足）+ -ary。sub + plere（満たす）。「補足の」。complete と同じ ple。

en: A person occupied with surveying: the process of determining positions on the earth's surface.
One who carries out a survey or poll.

surveyor.ety: From Middle English surveyour, from Anglo-Norman surveour, from Old French sorveor. By surface analysis, survey + -or.

note.ja: survey（見渡す・測量する）+ -or。sur（上から）+ videre（見る）。「測量士」。

en: A person's usual manner of thinking, behaving or reacting.
A tendency to become irritable or angry.

temperament.ety: Inherited from Middle English temperament, borrowed from Middle French tempérament, from Latin temperāmentum.

ex.en: Success often depends on one's temperament.
ex.ja: 成功不成功は気質に左右されることが多い。

ex.en: Nancy has a very lively and sweet temperament.
ex.ja: ナンシーはとても陽気でかわいらしい性格だ。

ex.en: Solvency is entirely a matter of temperament and not of income.
ex.ja: 支払能力は全く気質の問題であって、収入の問題ではない。

note.ja: ラテン語 temperamentum（ほどよい混合）から。temperare（混ぜ合わせる）。体液の混ざり具合で気質が決まると考えられた →「気質」。temperature と同じ。

en: The ordinal form of the number thirteen.
The person or thing in the thirteenth position.
One of thirteen equal parts of a whole.

thirteenth.ety: Inherited from Middle English thrittenthe, thrittethe, from Old English þrēottēoþa; equivalent to thirteen + -th (ordinal suffix).

ex.en: Tennis began in France in the thirteenth century.
ex.ja: テニスは１３世紀にフランスで始まった。

ex.en: Today is my thirteenth birthday.
ex.ja: 今日は私の１３歳の誕生日なんです。

ex.en: A few days after his thirteenth birthday, Tony left school, too.
ex.ja: １３歳の誕生日の２、３日後に、トニーも学校を卒業しました。

note.ja: thirteen + -th。「13番目」。

en: Lacking a top.
Very high; towering.
Not wearing any clothes on the upper body.
A convertible car having the top retracted or otherwise open.

en: Torture, originally as inflicted by an instrument of torture.
Any extreme pain, anguish or misery, either physical or mental.
To cause severe suffering to (stronger than to vex but weaker than to torture.)

torment.ety: From Middle English torment, from Old French torment, from Latin tormentum (“something operated by twisting”), from torquere (“to twist”). Compare native English bale (“suffering, woe, torment”) and English woe.

ex.en: I was a constant torment to my parents.
ex.ja: 私は両親の耐えない苦労の種だった。

ex.en: Father was tormented by my silly question.
ex.ja: 父は私の愚かな質問に苦しまれた。

ex.en: I'm tormented by the noise of traffic.
ex.ja: 車の騒音に悩まされています。

note.ja: ラテン語 tormentum（ねじって苦しめる道具）から。tort（ねじる）。→「苦痛・苦しめる」。

en: A usurper; one who gains power and rules extralegally, distinguished from kings elevated by election or succession.
A despot; a ruler who governs unjustly, cruelly, or harshly.
Tyrannical, tyrannous; like, characteristic of, or in the manner of a tyrant.
